source.title: RSASSA-PSS with SHA-256 under an RSA private key

requirements.quote: In a valid RSA private key with the first representation, the RSA modulus n is the same as in the corresponding RSA public key and is the product of u distinct odd primes r_i, i = 1, 2, ..., u, where u >= 2.
The RSA private exponent d is a positive integer less than n satisfying

In a valid RSA private key with the second representation, the two factors p and q are the first two prime factors of the RSA modulus n (i.e., r_1 and r_2); the CRT exponents dP and dQ are positive integers less than p and q, respectively, satisfying
and the CRT coefficient qInv is a positive integer less than p satisfying
It SHALL be 0 for this version of the document, unless multi-prime is used; in which case, it SHALL be 1.
It SHALL be omitted if version is 0 and SHALL contain at least one instance of OtherPrimeInfo if version is 1.
Version ::= INTEGER { two-prime(0), multi(1) } (CONSTRAINED BY {-- version MUST be multi if otherPrimeInfos present --})
If the message representative m is not between 0 and n - 1, output "message representative out of range" and stop.
Let s_1 = m^dP mod p and s_2 = m^dQ mod q.
Let h = (s_1 - s_2) * qInv mod p.
Let s = s_2 + q * h.
EM = EMSA-PSS-ENCODE (M, modBits - 1).
S = I2OSP (s, k).
If emLen < hLen + sLen + 2, output "encoding error" and stop.
Let mHash = Hash(M), an octet string of length hLen.
Generate a random octet string salt of length sLen; if sLen = 0, then salt is the empty string.
Let DB = PS || 0x01 || salt; DB is an octet string of length emLen - hLen - 1.
Let EM = maskedDB || H || 0xbc.
The length of the Salt MUST be equal to the length of the output of the digest algorithm.

clauses.title: the key's modulus and public exponent are those of its public key, and it has 2048 bits
the key is read from the given window of a larger array, whatever comes before or after it
flipping any one bit of the key makes it refused
flipping any one bit of p, q, dP, dQ or qInv makes the key refused
a key of version 1 or more is refused
a version 0 key with otherPrimeInfos after its coefficient is refused
a message representative of n or more is refused, and so is one not k octets long
0, 1 and n - 1 are their own signature representatives
RSASP1 of the octets 00 to ff is OpenSSL's
the empty-salt signature of "sample" is OpenSSL's
a signature verifies under the public key with SHA-256 and a 32-octet salt
the salt is 32 octets: a verifier told any other length refuses the signature
the salt is the SHA-256 of the label, d as k octets, and mHash
a signature with any salt of 0 to 222 octets verifies with that salt length
two different salts give two different signatures
a salt longer than emLen - hLen - 2 = 222 octets is an encoding error
flipping any one bit of the message makes the signature invalid
flipping any one bit of the signature makes it invalid
